title: Auditlog eviction, rehydration, and SLI playbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic operational playbook for audit log storage tiering, eviction/rehydration behavior, and SLI-driven backfill/replay patterns. It is intended for platform SREs, compliance engineers, and data-platform owners who run the audit-event pipeline and long-term storage.

Scope:
- Applies to audit/event streams (auth, admin actions, billing events, evidence blobs) that land in the central audit Kafka topic and are indexed into Elasticsearch / OpenSearch and long-term object store.
- Covers retention tiers (hot/warm/cold/archive), eviction triggers, rehydration paths, index mapping/versioning impact, backfill strategies, checkpointing, and common failure modes + runbook steps.

TL;DR decision points:
- 90 days hot writable index (fast search, low-latency queries).
- 365 days warm index (searchable but throttled; reduced replicas).
- >365 days -> compressed cold layer in object store (S3) with precomputed index shards for retrieval-by-request only.
- Eviction decisions driven by size and age SLOs, not just age. If daily index growth > projected by 25% re-evaluate quota or route to a temporary overflow index.

Retention SLOs (proposal):
- Ingestion SLA: 99.9% of audit events indexed within 30s of Kafka commit.
- Query availability: 99.5% for 0–90d, 95% for 90–365d, best-effort for >365d (rehydration on-demand within 4h).
- Data durability: 100% persisted to object store for >365d, with integrity checksum verification weekly.

Indexing architecture notes:
- Primary index per month named audit-YYYY-MM; rollover at 25GB or 24h, whichever first.
- Document id composition: <tenant>-<event-ts>-<kafka-offset>-<sha1(payload)> to maintain idempotency for re-ingest and avoid duplicate docs during backfills.
- Use a lightweight mapping optimized for common filters: timestamp, tenant_id, actor_id, action_type, resource_type, outcome_code. Avoid dynamic mappings for free-text fields; route long text to a separate blob store with pointer in the document.
- Shard strategy: small primary shards (10–20GB target) for balanced recovery. Allocate shard_count by projected month size / 15GB.

Eviction and compaction policy:
- Hot -> Warm: after 90d, reduce replicas to 1, move to less performant nodes, disable aggressive refresh (set refresh_interval=30s).
- Warm -> Cold/archive: run a compaction job that: 1) converts doc _source to compressed binary blob, 2) extracts indexable keys into a lightweight lookup index, 3) writes full payload to S3 with path audit/YYYY/MM/tenant/eventid.json.gz and a manifest.
- Eviction trigger conditions: age > policy OR cluster free space < 18% OR index write pressure beyond threshold. Eviction should be a controlled job with concurrency signals.

Rehydration (rehydration path and expectations):
- On-demand rehydrate flow: request -> check lightweight lookup index -> if not found, fetch from object store by manifest -> rehydrate into a temporary read-only index named rehydrate-<jobid>-<yyyyMMdd> -> expose via proxy to query subsystem. Goal: full document visible in queries within 4h for compliance requests.
- Bulk rehydrate (for backfills or audits): use the reindex-from-s3 tool with streaming decompress and idempotent writes; checkpoint every 10k documents.

Backfill and replay strategy (idempotent, resumable):
- Use kafka offset-driven replay: backfill process reads from topic start_offset -> target_offset; publishes a reingest marker per batch to control duplicates.
- All reindex jobs must store checkpoints in a durable store (Postgres or Dynamo) with keys: job_id, last_processed_offset, job_state, dry_run. Checkpoint freq: every 10k messages or 30s.
- Parallelization: partition backfills by tenant or by time-window. Keep per-partition ordering where required.
- Throttling: limit indexing throughput to avoid cluster OOM; autoscale worker count based on backpressure signals (queue depth, rejected execution).

Failure modes and remediation (short checklist):
- Consumer lag grows and never recovers:
  - Check DLQ volume, inspect consumer group offsets.
  - If Kafka retention expired, recover from object store snapshots and run rehydrate -> mark incident SEV2.
- Index shard corruption during reindex:
  - Stop reindex jobs immediately. Snapshot current index, set index.read_only, open a restore from last snapshot to a temp cluster, run consistency checks (doc counts, checksums). If corruption isolated to shard, reallocate shard from snapshot.
- Tombstone or delete spikes after RBAC v2 rollout:
  - Run sample query to identify TTL/deletion predicates, revert policy, and rehydrate deleted events from object store manifest for affected tenants.
- Manifest mismatch or missing payload in object store:
  - Verify manifest checksums; run integrity job that re-creates missing blobs from earliest available archive (if available). If permanently missing, escalate to Legal/Compliance.

Observability and SLIs (what to monitor):
- Ingestion latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99) from Kafka commit to ES index time.
- Consumer group lag in bytes and messages; alert P95 lag > 5m for more than 3m.
- Rehydrate job success ratio and average time-to-rehydrate.
- Storage growth delta vs projected; alert if monthly overrun > 15%.
- Index segment count and merge pressure; alert on sustained merge_throttle > threshold.

Runbook examples (common commands):
- check consumer lag:
  kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.service:9092 --describe --group audit-consumer
- reindex a month from s3 (dry-run):
  logs-reindexer --source s3://redwood-audit-archive/2024/11 --target es://audit-2024-11 --dry-run --checkpoint-store pg://reindex.checkpoints
- trigger ad-hoc rehydrate for tenant:
  POST /rehydrate?tenant=acme-corp&start=2024-11-01&end=2024-11-30 -> returns job_id.

Post-incident checklist:
- capture last successful checkpoint for all reindex jobs
- run parity check: compare expected doc counts (from kafka offsets) vs indexed docs
- produce short RCA with timelines, mitigation, and fixes for automation/alerts

Open action items:
- Finalize SLO numbers with Compliance and Product (pending).
- Add weekly integrity job to verify S3 manifests and checksums (owner: data-platform).
- Implement an automated throttling controller for reindex workers (owner: infra).

Notes and references:
- See JIRA-LOGS-517 for RBAC-v2 deletion regression test case.
- Reindexer repo: github.com/redwood-inference/logs-reindexer (PR#28 has S3 streaming patches).

Author notes: Draft leans toward conservative retention for quick compliance response while limiting hot storage spend. Want feedback from SRE and Legal on rehydrate SLA and escalation boundaries.
